summary: The comment opposes gutting the E-Rate program, arguing that it would devastate access for low-income and rural communities. It cites examples of how libraries and schools rely on E-Rate to provide internet access for students, job seekers, and business owners. The comment emphasizes the importance of internet access for education, employment, and civic engagement in these communities.

claims.argument: Gutting e-rate will devastate low income and rural communities
claims.evidence_quote: Gutting e-rate will devastate low income and rural communities. The members of these communities deserve equal access to the internet that other, wealthier communities have. As a librarian, I see every day how many people already struggle with affording their bills, let alone their internet bill. They rely on libraries and schools being able to provide reliable internet. Students need the internet to research and complete assignments. Job seekers need it to find work. Business owners need it to do all manner of administrative tasks. Not to mention how much of culture and civic life involves the internet these days. It is unconscionable to put their access at risk by gutting e-rate.
